earlier_scan.source_named: Bonnaud, Pierre 1992. Grammaire generale de l'auvergnat a l'usage des arvernisants (Cercle Terre d'Auvergne); fr.wikipedia classifies auvergnat as 'a accent d'intensite' but gives no placement

new_statements.quote: l'ACCENT TONIQUE, très important en auvergnat, car il est plus fort qu'en fr., il a deux positions courantes possibles (une seule en fr. : dernière syllabe) [...] Voici donc, relativement à l'écrit, les règles d'accentuation tonique du système nominal (tous les mots sauf les personnes conjuguées des verbes). La voix appuie sur la dernière syllabe des mots terminés par une consonne écrite (mais non prononcée), par -ï, -o, -ou, -u et par -â, -ê, -î (dans le cas de ces trois voyelles, l'accent circonflexe indique l'accent tonique final). elle appuie sur l'avant-dernière syllabe des mots terminés par -à (presque tous les fém. sing.), -a (fém. plur.), -e, -i. [...] les formes conjuguées du verbe ont une accentuation spéciale
new_statements.translation: the TONIC ACCENT, very important in Auvergnat, because it is stronger than in French, has two usual possible positions (only one in French: last syllable) [...] Here then, relative to the written form, are the rules of tonic accentuation of the nominal system (all words except the conjugated persons of verbs). The voice presses on the last syllable of words ending in a written (but unpronounced) consonant, in -ï, -o, -ou, -u and in -â, -ê, -î (for these three vowels the circumflex marks final tonic accent). It presses on the penultimate syllable of words ending in -à (almost all fem. sg.), -a (fem. pl.), -e, -i. [...] conjugated verb forms have a special accentuation
new_statements.citation: Bonnaud, Pierre. 1992. Grammaire générale de l'auvergnat à l'usage des arvernisants. Chamalières: Cercle Terre d'Auvergne (Collection Eubransa/Travaux).
new_statements.locator: pp. 15-16, section '3. Principes généraux', item 'Fonctionnalité' (règles d'accentuation tonique du système nominal); verb accentuation §54 D, pp. 146-147
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (329 pp., archive.org 'grammaire-bonnaud', text layer). Title page: Pierre BONNAUD, 'GRAMMAIRE GENERALE DE L'AUVERGNAT a l'usage des arvernisants', Cercle Terre d'Auvergne, Chamalieres (Collection Eubransa/Travaux) -- identity matches auve1240 (Auvergnat, ISO auv retired under oci); the Avertissement says it covers northern Auvergnat as base plus Cantal (Sanflorain) and Paulinois varieties, so it is the languoid, not a neighbour. The quoted passage is at PDF pp. 13-14 = printed pp. 15-16, in '3. Principes generaux' under the bullet 'Fonctionnalite': p. 15 bottom '-en aidant a placer correctement l'ACCENT TONIQUE, tres important en auvergnat, car il est plus fort qu'en fr., il a deux…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress falls on the final or the penultimate syllable, determined by the word's final segment (a Romance-type oxytone/paroxytone system): words ending in a consonant or in the vowels -ï, -o, -ou, -u, -â, -ê, -î and in final diphthongs/triphthongs are stressed on the last syllable; words ending in -à (fem. sg.), -a (fem. pl.), -e, -i are stressed on the penult. Conjugated verb forms follow a separate, tense- and person-based pattern (P1/2/6 penult; P4/5 final in central/southern Auvergnat; future/conditional/imperfect-2 final throughout; preterite penult throughout; northern Auvergnat regularising to penult per tense).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not discussed by Bonnaud. Dauzat 1897 (p. 40) mentions 'accents secondaires' only in passing; Dauzat 1906 p. 56 notes that in connected speech the long atonic final -as of plurals is 'à peu près aussi accentuée que la pénultième'.
new_statements.exceptions: Bonnaud: verb conjugation has its own rules (§54); -à + -d/-t (chàd, ràt, chantàd) is exceptionally tonic (p. 16); final triphthongs -aio/-aia are stressed on the last vowel unlike other triphthongs (p. 21); in western (Creuse-border) parlers a 'Limousin' shift moves stress onto the originally atonic plural ending (chantada) and stress may retract from a penultimate schwa (verjetei) (pp. 78, 310-311). Dauzat 1897/1906: numerous historical accent shifts (proparoxytone advance, retraction from final -é/-í/-u, hiatus shifts), varying by locality.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level, phonological word as written in Bonnaud's unified Auvergnat orthography; stated for words in isolation (nominal system) plus conjugated verb forms. Bonnaud's grammar is pan-Auvergnat (northern/Clermontois base with Sanflorain and Paulinois types). Dauzat's statements are for the patois of Vinzelles and the surrounding Basse-Auvergne region.
new_statements.identity_note: Bonnaud's grammar covers Auvergnat as a whole (northern/Clermontois base plus Sanflorain and Paulinois types; excludes Aurillac area). Dauzat 1897/1906 describe the Vinzelles patois and the Basse-Auvergne (Puy-de-Dôme) region only. Glottolog 5.1 files Auvergnat under Occitan [oci] (auve1240 is a Bookkeeping node); no separate glottocode for sub-dialects found.

sources.note: §130 p. 228 (Occitan as a whole, 'notre langue'): 'Sauf quelques cas particuliers très rares (v. § 409), notre langue n'admet l'accent que sur la dernière sillabe d'un mot ou sur l'avant-dernière'; p. 342 notes an Auvergnat 'déplacement d'accent' for -ia/-io words. General Occitan, Auvergnat only in passing.

sources.citation: Dauzat, Albert. 1906. Géographie phonétique d'une région de la Basse-Auvergne. Paris: Champion.
sources.note: Ch. I 'L'intensité', §I 'L'accent tonique', pp. 53-57: Latin accent persists in principle; regional shifts (proparoxytone advance everywhere; retraction from final short tonic -é, -í, -u in west/centre; long atonic finals -as attract accent, so in connected speech the final of plurals is 'à peu près aussi accentuée que la pénultième'; 1st/2nd pl. verb forms retract by analogy). Diachronic-dialectological, not a synchronic rule statement.

sources.citation: Dauzat, Albert. 1897. Études linguistiques sur la Basse-Auvergne. Phonétique historique du patois de Vinzelles (Puy-de-Dôme). Paris: F. Alcan.
sources.note: Troisième partie 'Accent tonique', pp. 109-111: 'L'accent tonique latin s'est généralement conservé'; diachronic account of shifts (proparoxytones became paroxytones at end of Middle Ages; hiatus shifts; retraction from final -é/-í); diphthongs 'toujours accentuées sur la première voyelle' (p. 40 area). Historical, one village (Vinzelles); no one-line synchronic rule.

sources.citation: Doniol, Henri. 1877. Les patois de la Basse-Auvergne: leur grammaire et leur littérature. Paris: Maisonneuve.
sources.note: pp. 25-27 discuss vowel qualities and proposed accent marks in spelling; remarks that 'l'accentuation... est la prosodie de chaque langue' but gives no stress-placement rule.
